items.name: 1 Leg Box Squat
items.instructions: This exercise requires a sturdy box or a chair. Simple stand ~6 inches in front of it and balance yourself on one leg. From here, begin squatting down in a smooth controlled motion while keeping your other leg straight out in front of you for balance. Slowly sit down on the box, pause for a 1 count and push back up with the working leg, while never letting your other leg touch the ground.

items.name: 1-Arm Half-Kneeling Lat Pulldown
items.instructions: Attach a D-Handle to a high pully. And use your lat muscles to pull the weight single handedly.

items.name: 1/2 Kneeling Thoracic Rotation
items.instructions:
• Begin in a half kneeling position with the
leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall
with a ball.
• With both hands directly in front of
you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach
the wall behind you.
• Exhale as you rotate, inhale
as you return to neutral and repeat.

Note: You will feel the mid-back and shoulder open with this exercise.
Note: Avoid rotating from your lower back. The motion should primarily be occurring in your mid-back

items.instructions: As a warmup, use light dumbbells, one in each hand. Lunge in alternating directions, forward, sideways, backwards and 45 degree angles.

items.name: 4-count burpees
items.instructions:
Starting position:

Stand straight, feet hip-width apart.

Steps:

1. Squat low and support yourself on the floor with your hands between the knees and in front of your feet, your back straight.
2. Keeping your hands on the floor, jump your legs backward into high plank position.
3. Jump your feet forward to return to the squat position.
4. Repeat.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.instructions:
Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you and the other leg bent at 90 degrees out to the side, so that the rear shin is parallel to the front shin. Keep your torso upright and, if possible, your hands off the floor.

Rotate both knees over to the other side so that the legs swap positions and you arrive in the same 90/90 position facing the opposite way. Move slowly and under control, keeping the feet in contact with the floor, and alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Mobility drill for internal and external rotation of the hips.

items.name: Lateral Rows on Cable, One Armed
items.instructions: Set cable at waist height, start with arm across your belly and move han over and out too other side, one arm at the time.

items.name: Lateral Walk
items.instructions: Lateral walks, also known as side steps or squat walks, are a type of exercise where you move sideways in a squatting position. They can be performed with or without resistance bands. These exercises strengthen the hip abductors, glutes, and other stabilizing muscles.

items.name: Lateral-to-Front Raises
items.instructions:
-(1) Perform a lateral raise, pausing at the top of the lift (2).

-Instead of lowering the weight, bring it to the front of your body so that you appear to be at the top position of a front raise.  You will do this by using a Pec Fly motion, maintaining straight arms. (3)

-Now lower the weight to your quadriceps, or, in other words, lower the dumbbells as though you are completing a Front Raise repetition. (4)

-Reverse the motion:  Perform a front raise (5), at the apex of the lift use a Reverse Fly motion to position the weights at the top of a Lateral Raise (6), and finally, lower the weights until your palms are essentially touching the sides of your thighs (7).  THIS IS ONE REP.

(1) l  front view(2) -l-  FV  (3) l-  side view   (4) l  SV/FV   (5) l-  SV (6) -l-  FV  (7)  l  FV/SV

items.name: Lean-Away Cable Lateral Raise
items.instructions:
Set a cable pulley at the lowest position and attach a single handle. Stand side-on to the machine, hold the frame with your near hand and lean your body away so you hang at an angle. With the far hand, grasp the handle in front of your hips and raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbow. Lower slowly. The lean increases tension on the side delts at the bottom of the movement. Complete all reps, then switch sides.

Note: Raise to shoulder height, no higher. Note: The lean is what keeps tension on the side delt at the bottom. Note: Hold the frame firmly and let your body hang away at a steady angle. Note: Lead with the elbow, keeping a slight bend in it.

items.name: Left levator scapulae stretch
items.instructions:
Starting position:

Start standing up or sitting down. Turn your head to the left, around 45 degrees or just above your nipple. Place your right hand behind your back or sit on it. Take your left hand and use it to hold the back of your head. Lean your head down slightly.

Steps:

1. After assuming the starting position, press your head against your left hand with slight force. Your hand should press back with equal force, so that your head doesn't move. Hold this position.

items.name: Left neck stretch
items.instructions:
Starting position:

Sit or stand with your back straight.

Steps:

1. Tilt your head to the side.
2. Take the hand closer to your head and use it to grab your head from the other side.
3. Push with your hand against your head and with your head against your hand so that the forces balance out and your head stays still.
4. Maintain this tension until the end of the exercise.

items.name: Leg and hip stretch
items.instructions: Gentle movements to improve the flexibility of the lower body and release tension in the hips.

items.name: Leg Curl
items.instructions: The leg curl, also known as the hamstring curl, is an isolation exercise that targets the hamstring muscles. The exercise involves flexing the lower leg against resistance towards the buttocks. Other exercises that can be used to strengthen the hamstrings are the glute-ham raise and the deadlift.

items.name: Leg curl with elastic
items.instructions: Standing position: Place the band under your feet in the middle of your foot and grasp it with a hammer grip.

items.name: Leg Curls (laying)
items.instructions: Lay on a bench and put your calves behind the leg holder (better if they are hold on around the lower calves). Hold a grip on the bars to make sure the body is firmly in place. Bend your legs bringing the weight up, go slowly back. During the exercise the body should not move, all work is done by the legs.

items.name: Windshield Wipers
items.instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar, raise your legs to the ceiling. Move lower body from left to right with straight legs like a windshield wiper

items.name: Wrist circles
items.instructions:
Wrist circles is warm-up exercise, where you rotate your wrists in a circular motion. They improve mobility and are recommended before exercises such as pull ups, hand stands and other exercises that put pressure on your wrists.

Note: Rotate one time in both directions per rep

items.name: Wrist curl, cable
items.instructions:
1. Extend your arm down, then slightly lift your forearm
2. Extend your wrist in a supinated form (palm up)
3. Adjust cable height so that the cable handle is in your supinated hand
4. Perform the movement by
curling your palms and wrists upwards
5. (optional/variable) Pause at the top
6. Slowly return to the starting position

items.name: Wrist curl, dumbbells
items.instructions:
1. Sitting on a bench, grab the dumbbell with your palms facing up
and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs
and allow your wrists to hang over your knees.
2. Perform the movement by
curling your palms and wrists towards your face.
3. (optional/variable) Pause at the top.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.

items.name: YTW Raises
items.instructions:
The YTW exercise for scapular retraction is designed to strengthen the inter-scapular muscles between your shoulder blades, to help retract or pull your shoulders back, helping to maintain proper upright posture.

Note: Start in neutral standing posture.
Note: Bring your arms up to roughly 135 degrees for the Y position, slightly in front of you, then bring your arms backwards by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Note: Concentrate on squeezing the shoulder blade or scapula contraction at the end range of motion, holding this position for 3-5 seconds. Then release.
Note: Bring your arms down to roughly 90 degrees, rotate your thumbs outwards, and bring your arms backwards by squeezing your shoulder blades again with scapular retraction.
Note: For the W component, keep your arms around 90 degrees, but bring them backwards in a slight W position
Note: squeezing at the end range-focusing on the middle and lower inter-scapular fibers.

items.name: YWTs
items.instructions:
*Starting position:
Lie down, preferably on a mat. Stretch your arms above your head in a "Y" position (arms pointing up diagonally at around 45 degrees). Your thumbs should be pointing up.
Steps:*

1. With arms in the Y position, lift your chest slightly from the ground, creating a pull tension in your arms upward.
2. Hold this position for several seconds (15-30 is ideal).
3. Keeping your chest up, bend at your elbows to move from a Y position to a "W" position, with arms bent at the elbows and maintaining the upward tension.
4. Hold for around as long as with the Y position.
5. Still with your chest up, move to a "T" position, straightening your arms out to the side to be perpendicular to your body.
6. Hold for around as long as you held the W position.
7. Move from the T position to the W position, then from the W position to the Y position.
8. Repeat.

items.name: Zottman curl
items.instructions: With your palms facing forward, curl the weights up to your shoulders. Turn your hands so that that your palms downwards and slowly return the weights back down. Finally face your palms back forward.

items.instructions: Jump wide, then close

items.name: Squat Sky Reach Stretch
items.instructions:
1. Drop into a squat.
2. Hold one ankle with the opposite hand.
3. Fold your other arm to your chest.
4. Staying in the squat and keeping hold of your ankle, twist to turn your chest-hand back/outwards until your elbow is pointing at the sky.
5. Return to the neutral squatting position with your hand on your chest. Repeat movement as required.

Repeat on both sides.

Note: If you can, at the top of the stretch uncoil your arm and reach your hand for the sky, returning your hand to your chest on the way down.

items.name: Squat Thrust
items.instructions: The burpee, or squat thrust, is a full body exercise used in strength training and as an aerobic exercise. The basic movement is performed in four steps and known as a four-count burpee: Begin in a standing position. Move into a squat position with your hands on the ground. (count 1) Kick your feet back into a plank position, while keeping your arms extended. (count 2) Immediately return your feet into squat position. (count 3) Stand up from the squat position (count 4)

items.name: Squats
items.instructions:
Place a barbell in a rack just below shoulder-height. Dip under the bar to put it behind the neck across the top of the back, and grip the bar with the hands wider than shoulder-width apart. Lift the chest up and squeeze the shoulder blades together to keep the straight back throughout the entire movement. Stand up to bring the bar off the rack and step backwards, then place the feet so that they are a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Sit back into hips and keep the back straight and the chest up, squatting down so the hips are below the knees. From the bottom of the squat, press feet into the ground and push hips forward to return to the top of the standing position.

Note: Make a pause at the bottom of 1sec, at the top, 3
Note: Go down till your thighs are parallel to the floor

items.name: Barbell Full Squat
items.instructions:
The barbell full squat is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups in the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.
Proper form is crucial for maximizing results and preventing injuries during the barbell full squat. This includes maintaining a shoulder-width stance, creating whole body tension, controlling your descent, and maintaining proper depth and knee positioning.
Assistance moves such as the front squat, goblet squat, split squat, and Bulgarian split squat can help improve your performance in the barbell full squat by targeting specific muscle groups and improving overall technique.
To *achieve new personal records in your back squat, gradually increase weight over time, vary rep ranges and sets to stimulate muscle growth, and prioritize rest and recovery* between training sessions.

Note: Start by positioning your feet shoulder-width apart, with toes slightly turned outwards.

items.name: Barbell Hack Squats
items.instructions: Perform leg squats with barbell behind your legs

items.name: Belt Squat
items.instructions: Belt Squat: a squat variation done with a belt attached to a loading machine or platform so the weight is supported at the hips instead of on the spine. It mainly trains the quads and glutes, with much less lower-back fatigue than a barbell squat. Use a full range of motion, keep the torso upright, and drive through the mid-foot.

items.name: Squat (Stacchi)
items.instructions:
1. Stai con i piedi alla larghezza delle spalle
2. Sposta i fianchi indietro e piega le ginocchia e i fianchi per abbassare il busto
3. Ripeti

items.name: Squat a pistola a destra
items.instructions:
1. Stai in piedi su una gamba, con l'altra gamba dritta e leggermente in avanti.
2. Piegare un ginocchio lentamente, scendendo in uno squat e mantenendo la schiena e l'altra gamba dritta.
3. Alzati lentamente dallo squat, raddrizzando il ginocchio piegato e mantenendo l'altra gamba dritta.
4. Ripeti

items.name: Squat a pistola a sinistra
items.instructions:
1. Stai in piedi su una gamba, con l'altra gamba dritta e leggermente in avanti.
2. Piegare un ginocchio lentamente, scendendo in uno squat e mantenendo la schiena e l'altra gamba dritta.
3. Alzati lentamente dallo squat, raddrizzando il ginocchio piegato e mantenendo l'altra gamba dritta.
4. Ripeti

items.name: Squat box
items.instructions:
1. *Preparare il box:Posizionate il box dietro di voi, a circa un metro e mezzo da un rack per lo squat se utilizzate un bilanciere. Scegliete un'altezza che vi consenta di accovacciarvi e di battere delicatamente i glutei sul box con la schiena dritta.
2. In piedi, con una forma corretta:State in piedi con i piedi alla larghezza delle spalle e le punte dei piedi leggermente rivolte verso l'esterno. Impegnate il core e mantenete la schiena neutra. Se si utilizza un bilanciere, posizionarlo all'altezza delle spalle.
3. Abbassarsi:Sedetevi come se doveste sedervi su una sedia, piegando le ginocchia e abbassando i fianchi verso il box. Mantenete il core teso e la schiena dritta durante tutto il movimento.
4. Discesa controllata:Scendere in modo controllato finché i glutei non toccano delicatamente il box. Non buttatevi a terra.
5. Pausa e rialzo:* Fate una breve pausa sul fondo con la schiena dritta e il core impegnato. Quindi, premere sui talloni per risalire alla posizione di partenza.

Migliora la coordinazione, l'equilibrio e la resistenza, tonifica i muscoli delle gambe e dei glutei e aumenta la densità ossea eliminando il rischio di osteoporosi.

items.name: Squat laterale sinistro
items.instructions:
1. Stai in piedi e fai un ampio passo laterale, appena superiore alla larghezza delle spalle.
2. Piega un ginocchio finché la coscia non è parallela al pavimento. Il ginocchio piegato deve essere in linea con il piede.
3. Spingi indietro alla posizione di partenza e ripetere.

items.name: Squat laterali a destra
items.instructions:
1. Stai in piedi e fai un ampio passo laterale, appena superiore alla larghezza delle spalle.
2. Piega un ginocchio finché la coscia non è parallela al pavimento. Il ginocchio piegato deve essere in linea con il piede.
3. Spingi indietro alla posizione di partenza e ripetere.

items.name: Squat laterali a sinistra
items.instructions:
1. Stai con la schiena dritta
2. Fai un grande passo in avanti con la gamba sinistra
3. Abbassa il bacino fino a toccare quasi il pavimento con il ginocchio destro
4. Riporta il bacino verso l'alto
5. Ripetere dal passaggio 3.

items.name: Squat sumo
items.instructions:
Posizione di partenza:

Stare in piedi con le gambe larghe e le dita dei piedi rivolte verso l'esterno.

Passi:

1. Sprofondare lentamente piegando le ginocchia in fuori. Portare le braccia in avanti. Tenere la testa, il petto e i fianchi in linea retta. Stringere i glutei.
2. Spingete verso l'alto nella posizione di partenza.
3. Ripetere questo esercizio con un movimento pulsante.

items.name: Spinte squat
items.instructions:
Posizione di partenza:

Iniziare in posizione di plank alto:schiena, braccia e gambe dritte e mani alla larghezza delle spalle.

Passi:

1. Saltare i piedi in avanti tra le braccia, mantenendo la schiena piatta.
2. Tenendo le mani sul pavimento, saltare le gambe indietro in posizione di plank alto.
3. Ripetere.

items.name: Panca declinata con bilanciere
items.instructions: Sdraiatevi su una panca declinata, il bilanciere deve trovarsi direttamente sopra gli occhi, le ginocchia sono leggermente angolate e i piedi sono ben saldi sul pavimento. Concentratevi, respirate profondamente e afferrate la sbarra a più della larghezza delle spalle. Portatela lentamente verso il basso fino a sfiorare brevemente il petto all'altezza dei capezzoli. Spingere il bilanciere verso l'alto.

items.name: Panca inclinata con manubri
items.instructions:
La panca dovrebbe essere inclinata ovunque da 30 a 45 gradi

Assicurati di premere i manubri verso l'alto (perpendicolarmente al pavimento)

items.name: Panca Piana con Manubri
items.instructions:
Il movimento è molto simile a quello della panca con bilanciere, ma il peso viene portato al petto in un punto più basso.
Impugnate due manubri e sdraiatevi su una panca. Tenete i pesi vicino al petto, all'altezza dei capezzoli, e spingeteli verso l'alto fino a tendere le braccia. Lasciare scendere il peso lentamente e in modo controllato.

items.name: Panca piana con presa srtetta
items.instructions: Sdraiatevi su una panca, il bilanciere è direttamente sopra gli occhi, le ginocchia formano un leggero angolo e i piedi sono ben saldi a terra. Impugnare la sbarra con una presa stretta (circa 20 cm). Portare il peso lentamente verso il basso fino a quando le braccia sono parallele al pavimento (gomito: angolo retto), premere poi il bilanciere verso l'alto. Quando si porta il bilanciere verso il basso, non farlo scendere sui capezzoli come nel normale esercizio di panca, ma un po' più in basso.

items.name: Addominali su panca inclinata
items.instructions: Sdraiarsi sulla schiena su una panca inclinata, i piedi sono su un'estremità della panca. Chiedete a un compagno o utilizzate un altro aiuto (bilanciere, ecc.) per tenerli fissi, le mani sono dietro la testa. Da questa posizione, muovete il busto verso l'alto finché la testa o i gomiti non toccano le ginocchia. Eseguire questo movimento arrotolando la schiena.

items.name: Croci con Manubri su Panca Declinata
items.instructions:
L'esercizio è lo stesso di una panca normale:
Prendi due manubri e sdraiati su una panca, assicurati che i piedi
siano ben saldi a terra e che la schiena non sia arcuata, ma abbia un
buon contatto con la panca. Le braccia sono tese davanti a te,
all'incirca alla larghezza delle spalle. Piega ora un po' le braccia e
abbassale lateralmente con un movimento a semicerchio. Senza modificare
l'angolo del gomito, riportali indietro con un movimento fluido.

items.name: Croci su panca Inclinata
items.instructions: Croci su panca InclinataCroci su panca Inclinata

items.name: Croci su panca piana
items.instructions: Afferra un manubrio di peso moderato in modo che i palmi delle mani siano piatti contro la parte inferiore delle piastre superiori e i pollici siano attorno alla barra. Sdraiati sulla schiena su una panca piana in modo che solo la parte superiore della schiena e le spalle siano a contatto con la panca. I tuoi piedi dovrebbero essere posizionati alla larghezza delle spalle e la tua testa dovrebbe pendere leggermente verso il basso. Con il manubrio appoggiato a distanza di un braccio direttamente sul petto, piega le braccia di circa 15 gradi e tienile piegate per tutto il movimento. Abbassa lentamente il manubrio all'indietro e verso il basso in un arco di semicerchio nella posizione più bassa possibile. Sollevalo lentamente lungo lo stesso arco fino al punto di partenza e ripeti per il numero richiesto di ripetizioni.

items.name: Curl su Panca a 45°
items.instructions: Posiziona la barra EZ curl sulle maniglie di riposo davanti alla panca del predicatore. Appoggiati alla panca e afferra la barra EZ curl con i palmi rivolti verso l'alto. Sedersi sulla panca del predicatore in modo che la parte superiore delle braccia poggi sulla parte superiore dell'imbottitura e il petto sia premuto contro l'imbottitura. Abbassa il peso finché i gomiti non sono estesi e le braccia sono dritte. Riporta i pesi al punto di partenza contraendo i bicipiti. Ripetere

items.name: Bench Press
items.instructions:
Lay down on a bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.

If you train with a high weight it is advisable to have a spotter that can help you up if you can't lift the weight on your own.

With the width of the grip you can also control which part of the chest is trained more:

wide grip: outer chest muscles
narrow grip: inner chest muscles and triceps

Note: Don't stretch your arms completly

items.name: Bench Press Isometric
items.instructions: A bench press isometric hold is a static strength exercise where you pause and hold a barbell or dumbbells either at your chest, mid-press, or at lockout without moving for a set time

items.name: Bench Press Narrow Grip
items.instructions:
• *Setup:Lie flat on the bench and grip the bar at shoulder-width (closer than a standard bench press).
• Descent:Lower the bar with control to your lower chest.
• Form:Keep your elbows tucked in tight against your torso: do not let them flare out.
• Ascent:* Press the bar straight back up, squeezing your triceps at the top.

items.name: DB Underhand bench press
items.instructions: Underhand grip DB, perform a normal bench press movement, keeping the elbows close to the chest

items.name: Decline Bench Press Barbell
items.instructions: Lay down on a decline bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.

items.name: Decline Bench Press Dumbbell
items.instructions: Take two dumbbells and sit on a decline bench, the feet are firmly on the floor, the head is resting the bench. Hold the weights next to the chest, at the height of your nipples and press them up till the arms are stretched. Let the weight slowly and controlled down.

items.name: Dumbbell close grip bench press
items.instructions:
Lie down with your back on a flat bench. Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Raise your arms towards the ceiling with your palms facing each other and dumbbells pressed together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells to your chest, then slowly push them back. Repeat the exercise.

items.name: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press
items.instructions: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press, chest press movement focusing on the triceps. DB stays parallel with body

items.name: Incline Bench Press - Barbell
items.instructions: To do slowly, tempo is 4010

items.name: Incline Bench Press - Dumbbell
items.instructions:
This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso.

1. Bench Adjustment and Preparation: Set the bench to an incline of between 30 and 45 degrees (an incline greater than 45° will place too much strain on the shoulders and reduce the stimulus to the chest). Sit down with a dumbbell on each thigh.

2. Starting position: Lean back, resting your back against the bench, while using your knees one after the other to push the dumbbells upward to shoulder height.

3. Anatomical Stabilization: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your scapulas (bring your shoulder blades together and press them into the bench) to protect your shoulders and stabilize the load.

4. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells slowly and in a controlled manner toward the upper part of your chest. Your elbows should not splay out to the sides (90°); maintain a safe angle of about 45 to 60 degrees relative to your torso.

5. Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the dumbbells vertically upward as you exhale. Follow a slightly converging path (without letting them touch at the top). Stop the movement just before locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension in the upper pectoral.

items.name: Leg curl con elastico

items.name: Alternating bicep curls
items.instructions:
Starting position:

Start standing up with dumbbells in each hand, your back straight and feet hip-width apart. Your arms should be relaxed, pointing down. Your knees should be slightly bent, your abs contracted, and your shoulders down.

Steps:

1. Bend one arm at the elbow, bringing the dumbbell up to your shoulder. Your upper arm should remain motionless during this movement.
2. Bring the dumbbell back down until your arm is in its original relaxed position.
3. Repeat, switching arms.

items.instructions: Stand with your knees slightly bent and your back straight. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, using a neutral grip at your sides.

items.name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
items.instructions:
Sitting on a bench, grab a barbell with your palms facing down and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs and allow your wrists to hang over your knees.

Curl your knuckles towards your face, lifting the barbell. Pause for a moment in the top position, then slowly return the barbell to the starting position.

items.name: Barbell Wrist Curl
items.instructions:
Sitting on a bench, grab a barbell with your palms facing up and your hands shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs and allow your wrists to hang over your knees. Perform the movement by curling your palms and wrists towards your face.

Pause for a moment in the top position, then slowly return the barbell to the starting position.

items.name: Bayesian Curl
items.instructions: Cable curl with stretched shoulder (backwards)

items.name: Biceps Curl Machine
items.instructions: The biceps curl machine is designed to isolate the biceps muscles and provide a controlled range of motion. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and adjust the seat so your arms are aligned with the machine's handles or pads. Grip the handles firmly, keeping your elbows fixed in place, and curl the handles upward by contracting your biceps. Slowly lower the handles to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.

items.name: Biceps Curl With Cable
items.instructions:
Stand around 30 - 40cm away from the cable, the feet are firmly on the floor. Take the bar and lift the weight with a fast movements. Lower the weight as with the dumbbell curls slowly and controlled.

Note: Don't move the elbows during the exercise

items.name: Biceps Curls With SZ-bar
items.instructions:
Hold the SZ-bar shoulder-wide, the back is straight, the shoulders slightly back, the arms are streched. Bend the arms, bringing the weight up, with a fast movement. Without pausing, let down the bar with a slow and controlled movement.

Don't allow your body to swing during the exercise, all work is done by the biceps, which are the only mucles that should move (pay attention to the elbows).

Note: Fluid movements with no pauses at the top or the bottom

items.name: 1 Leg Box Squat
items.instructions: This exercise requires a sturdy box or a chair. Simple stand ~6 inches in front of it and balance yourself on one leg. From here, begin squatting down in a smooth controlled motion while keeping your other leg straight out in front of you for balance. Slowly sit down on the box, pause for a 1 count and push back up with the working leg, while never letting your other leg touch the ground.

items.name: 90/90 Hamstring / Barre-Style Stretch

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.instructions:
Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you and the other leg bent at 90 degrees out to the side, so that the rear shin is parallel to the front shin. Keep your torso upright and, if possible, your hands off the floor.

Rotate both knees over to the other side so that the legs swap positions and you arrive in the same 90/90 position facing the opposite way. Move slowly and under control, keeping the feet in contact with the floor, and alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Mobility drill for internal and external rotation of the hips.

items.name: Abduction while standing
items.instructions:
Training a stable stance, predominantly on one leg, is crucial for both sides. On the one hand, it prevents discomfort and, on the other, it establishes a stable foundation. The practitioner assumes the usual standing position and, with a stable upper body, attempts to repeatedly lift the unloaded leg, bend it at the hip and knee, and then lower it again. The movement is also repeated on the other side. The exercise trains the stability of the hip-surrounding muscles.

Note: stabiler Oberkörper

items.name: Adductor Rock Backs
items.instructions:
Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot flat on the floor and the toes pointing forward.

Keep your back flat and slowly push your hips back towards the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inside of the extended leg. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs.

Mobility exercise for the adductors and the hips.

items.name: Arabesque
items.instructions: Take all your weight onto one leg and you're going to maintain that position, keeping your hips and pelvis level the whole time. With your back in a neutral position you want to tilt yourself forward kicking your leg back up and then slowly with your glutes bring yourself back up to neutral.

items.name: Band Terminal Knee extension
items.instructions: This is an end range strengthening exercise for the knee extensors. Start by looping a band around the back of one knee and anchoring the other end to a stable surface in front of you. Stand in a split stance with the banded knee bent and placed as the front leg. Straighten the knee to pull against the bands resistance and maintain a contraction in your quadriceps for up to 5 seconds before releasing.

items.name: Bulgarian Squat with Dumbbells
items.instructions: The Bulgarian split squat consists of performing a squat on one leg with the rear foot resting on a raised platform. Elevating your back leg on a bench creates instability and increases the range of motion of the exercise.

items.name: Chest-Supported Rear Delt Raise
items.instructions: "The Y"Position: Set an incline bench to 30-45 degrees. Lie face-down with your chest supported, keeping your head neutral or looking slightly down to avoid neck strain.Grip: Hold light dumbbells with a neutral or thumbs-up grip (thumb pointing to the ceiling).Movement: With straight or slightly bent elbows, raise the dumbbells up and out in a "Y" shape. Focus on moving the shoulders and shoulder blades rather than just lifting the arms.Top Position: Squeeze the shoulder blades together and reach high, ensuring the arms are angled to form a "Y".Control: Lower the dumbbells slowly to the starting position.

items.name: Croci con Manubri su Panca Declinata
items.instructions:
L'esercizio è lo stesso di una panca normale:
Prendi due manubri e sdraiati su una panca, assicurati che i piedi
siano ben saldi a terra e che la schiena non sia arcuata, ma abbia un
buon contatto con la panca. Le braccia sono tese davanti a te,
all'incirca alla larghezza delle spalle. Piega ora un po' le braccia e
abbassale lateralmente con un movimento a semicerchio. Senza modificare
l'angolo del gomito, riportali indietro con un movimento fluido.

items.instructions: Croci su panca InclinataCroci su panca Inclinata

items.name: Croci su panca piana
items.instructions: Afferra un manubrio di peso moderato in modo che i palmi delle mani siano piatti contro la parte inferiore delle piastre superiori e i pollici siano attorno alla barra. Sdraiati sulla schiena su una panca piana in modo che solo la parte superiore della schiena e le spalle siano a contatto con la panca. I tuoi piedi dovrebbero essere posizionati alla larghezza delle spalle e la tua testa dovrebbe pendere leggermente verso il basso. Con il manubrio appoggiato a distanza di un braccio direttamente sul petto, piega le braccia di circa 15 gradi e tienile piegate per tutto il movimento. Abbassa lentamente il manubrio all'indietro e verso il basso in un arco di semicerchio nella posizione più bassa possibile. Sollevalo lentamente lungo lo stesso arco fino al punto di partenza e ripeti per il numero richiesto di ripetizioni.

items.name: Curl  - With Shoulder Elevated

items.name: Curl Bicipiti Alternato con Manubrio
items.instructions:
Impugnare due bilancieri, le braccia sono distese, le mani sono sul fianco, i palmi rivolti verso l'interno. Piegare un braccio alla volta e portare il peso con un movimento veloce verso l'alto. Allo stesso tempo, ruotate le braccia di 90 gradi all'inizio del movimento. Nel punto più alto, ruotate un po' il peso verso l'esterno. Senza fare pause, riportare il braccio verso il basso, lentamente, e fare lo stesso con l'altro braccio.
Non lasciate che il corpo oscilli durante l'esercizio, tutto il lavoro è svolto dai bicipiti, che sono gli unici muscoli che devono muoversi (fate attenzione ai gomiti).

items.instructions: This exercise involves lifting a barbell from the ground to the shoulders, then pressing it overhead. items.name: Bear Walk 2
items.instructions:
-Rest your weight on your palms and the balls of your feet, not dissimilar to normal pushup position

-Move as fast as you can.  Measure your reps/sets in either distance (i.e. 40 yards) or time (i.e. 45 seconds)

items.name: Bench Press
items.instructions:
Lay down on a bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.

If you train with a high weight it is advisable to have a spotter that can help you up if you can't lift the weight on your own.

With the width of the grip you can also control which part of the chest is trained more:

wide grip: outer chest muscles
narrow grip: inner chest muscles and triceps

Note: Don't stretch your arms completly

items.name: Benchpress Dumbbells
items.instructions:
1. Setup and Starting Position: Sit at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting vertically against each thigh. Carefully lean back while driving the dumbbells toward your chest with your knees.

2. The “Leg Drive” and Posture: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your shoulder blades (press them together against the bench) and maintain a slight natural lumbar curve.

3. Starting Position: Push the dumbbells toward the ceiling. Your wrists should be aligned with your elbows. Rotate the dumbbells slightly inward (about 45 degrees) so that your elbows do not splay out too far to the sides, thereby protecting your shoulders.

4. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner toward the sides of your chest. Your elbows should lower at an angle of about 45-60 degrees relative to your body. Feel the stretch in the lower part of your chest.

5. Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the weight upward in a slight arc (toward the center), without letting the dumbbells collide at the top or fully locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension. Exhale as you lift.

items.name: Row
items.instructions: In strength training, rowing (or a row, usually preceded by a qualifying adjective: for instance a seated row) is an exercise where the purpose is to strengthen the muscles that draw the rower's arms toward the body (latissimus dorsi) as well as those that retract the scapulae (trapezius and rhomboids) and those that support the spine (erector spinae). When done on a rowing machine, rowing also exercises muscles that extend and support the legs (quadriceps and thigh muscles). In all cases, the abdominal and lower back muscles must be used in order to support the body and prevent back injury.

items.name: Rowing seated, narrow grip

Tighten muscles
Controlled movement
Slow movement
Keep upper body upright
Do not lean back
Pull toward chest

Note: Pull the weight towards your belly button, not further up

items.name: Rowing, T-bar
items.instructions:
The execution of this exercise is very similar to the regular bent over rowing, only that the bar is fixed here.

Grab the barbell with a wide grip (slightly more than shoulder wide) and lean forward. Your upper body is not quite parallel to the floor, but forms a slight angle. The chest's out during the whole exercise. Pull now the barbell with a fast movement towards your belly button, not further up. Go slowly down to the initial position. Don't swing with your body and keep your arms next to your body.

Note: Don't arch your back!
Note: Go somewhat down in your knees and pull back

items.name: Alternating High Cable Row
items.instructions:
1. Start
by putting the attachment in a high position on the cable station and step back about 1m from the attachment. Grab
the cable pulley handle in your left hand at about head height with your elbow slightly bent. Step back with your left foot.
2. Pull
your elbow joint in toward the torso twisting slightly and perform a
single-arm row. Engage the lats as you twist.
3. Return
to the starting position with cable pulley and left foot and grab the cable pulley handle in the right
hand. Repeat this motion on the opposite side with your right foot stepped back.

Note: Use your core strength for stability and keep spine stable for all repetitions.
Note: Focus on taking the lats through their entire range of motion in this cable pulley movement.

With dumbbells in hand, bend at the hip until hands hang just below the knees (similar to straight-legged-deadlift starting position). Note: Keep your wrist neutral and aligned with your forearm

result.name: Braced Squat
result.instructions:
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, while standing as tall as you can.

Grab a weight plate and hold it out in front of your body with arms straight out. Keep your core tight and stand with a natural arch in your back.

Now, push hips back and bend knees down into a squat as far as you can. Hold for a few moments and bring yourself back up to the starting position.

result.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat

Squat down until thighs are parallel to floor. Keep back straight, bend and move hips backward to keep knees above feet. Return, keep knees slightly flexed. Repeat.

Keep bodyweight on heels and look ahead or slightly above to keep back straight.

result.name: Hindu Squats

As you descend towards the floor, raise your heels off the ground, while keeping your back as vertical  as possible.

Upon attaining the bottom position, touch the hands to the heels.

Then stand up ending with the heels on the ground, arms extended in front of the chest then rowing into the start position.

1. Setup and Starting Position: Sit at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting vertically against each thigh. Carefully lean back while driving the dumbbells toward your chest with your knees.

2. The “Leg Drive” and Posture: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your shoulder blades (press them together against the bench) and maintain a slight natural lumbar curve.

3. Starting Position: Push the dumbbells toward the ceiling. Your wrists should be aligned with your elbows. Rotate the dumbbells slightly inward (about 45 degrees) so that your elbows do not splay out too far to the sides, thereby protecting your shoulders.

4. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner toward the sides of your chest. Your elbows should lower at an angle of about 45-60 degrees relative to your body. Feel the stretch in the lower part of your chest.

5. Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the weight upward in a slight arc (toward the center), without letting the dumbbells collide at the top or fully locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension. Exhale as you lift.

result.name: Incline Bench Press - Dumbbell
result.instructions:
This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso.

1. Bench Adjustment and Preparation: Set the bench to an incline of between 30 and 45 degrees (an incline greater than 45° will place too much strain on the shoulders and reduce the stimulus to the chest). Sit down with a dumbbell on each thigh.

2. Starting position: Lean back, resting your back against the bench, while using your knees one after the other to push the dumbbells upward to shoulder height.

3. Anatomical Stabilization: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your scapulas (bring your shoulder blades together and press them into the bench) to protect your shoulders and stabilize the load.

4. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells slowly and in a controlled manner toward the upper part of your chest. Your elbows should not splay out to the sides (90°); maintain a safe angle of about 45 to 60 degrees relative to your torso.

5. Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the dumbbells vertically upward as you exhale. Follow a slightly converging path (without letting them touch at the top). Stop the movement just before locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension in the upper pectoral.
